chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who killed his slave. He said: 'He emancipes a neck, and fasts for two consecutive months, and repents to Allah.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for killing one's own slave, requiring emancipation, two months of consecutive fasting, and repentance. While similar to the general kaffarah for accidental killing in Surah An-Nisa, Shia scholars note the distinct emphasis on the slave-owner's personal accountability and the mandatory nature of consecutive fasting as a form of spiritual purification. The parallel narration via Yunus and Zur'a reinforces the reliability of this ruling within the Imami tradition.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who kills a slave of his. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He emancipates a neck, and Fasts for two months consecutively, and repents to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama’at - similar to it’.
